text:
maya: Ran an nsys + perfetto pass on staging for the 7B route. Seeing a KV-cache miss spike that correlates with larger batches (batch 16+). attaching the perfetto link and a quick nsys timeline: https://perfetto.app/trace/xyz
prashant: Can you paste the nsys summary? curious which GPU kernel got selected when the spike happens — int8 vs fp16?
eva: if possible add NVTX ranges around: 1) KV prefetch 2) kernel-selection & kernel-launch 3) decode loop boundary. right now the timeline lumps them together and we can't tell if it's selector overhead or actual kernel latency.
maya: paste of the nsys summary excerpt:
```
GPU_KERNELS:
 - cudaKernelPack: 12.3ms
 - aten::linalg_gemm: 51.2ms (selected: turing_opt_int8)
 - kv_prefetch_async: 8.7ms
```
The weird part: when batch grows, kv_prefetch_async jumps to 30ms but KV hit rate doesn't drop proportionally.
jamal: Could be prefetch contention or wrong prefetch window. Also, NVTX ranges currently we have are very coarse: "request" and "model_infer" only. We should add per-request sub-spans, but keep them compact.
eva: Agreed. Proposal for NVTX naming (short + parseable): `req:<rid>:kv:prefetch`, `req:<rid>:selector`, `req:<rid>:kernellaunch[:shard]`, `req:<rid>:decode`. Use short request id (first 8 chars of req hash). That keeps trace size down.
prashant: Two instrumentation notes: 1) don't emit per-token NVTX ranges (trace explosion). 2) emit integer tags for op type and model variant (nvtxRangePushEx with payload) so our trace post-processor can aggregate without parsing strings.
maya: example gRPC runtime patch I used (C++):
```
std::string rid = request.id.substr(0,8);
nvtxRangePushA(("req:"+rid+":kv:prefetch").c_str());
kv_prefetch(keys);
nvtxRangePop();
```
Works but worried about the string alloc overhead in hot path.
jamal: allocate a small stack buffer and fmt into it, or use nvtxRangeStartEx with precomputed id -> int. We should centralize a tiny helper: `nvtx_scoped_range(req_short, tag_enum)` in runtime to avoid repeated logic.
perf-bot: autotest results: added KV-prefetch NVTX ranges (dev branch) — trace size +3.2%, 99th p90 overhead measured ~0.8ms for small batches, ~1.6ms for batch16 due to string allocs.
eva: that matches expectation. Two follow-ups: a) add option to compile-time strip NVTX for perf-sensitive builds, b) change helper to use static char buffer + snprintf to avoid heap.
prashant: Also check kernel selector path: when selector chooses int8 we see an extra `quantize` prep kernel launching. That kernel is cheap normally but seems serialized with prefetch for some sequences. Try moving prefetch to happen earlier (prefetch window = tokens + 4) or make it asynchronous with separate CUDA stream.
maya: I'll run another nsys job with: - nvtx per-request spans (short IDs), - prefetch on separate stream, - perfetto sampling at 100us, and capture kernel selection tags. Will post results in this thread.
jamal: one more ask: include a tiny artifact in trace metadata with `model_variant` and `selector_version` so we can filter traces by selector config without looking at timelines. nvtxRange's payload or perfetto trace config metadata works.
eva: +1. Also think about a post-processing script to collapse repeated per-request ranges into a single summary line (reduce trace noise for dashboards).
maya: ok thanks — kicking off run now. assigning follow-ups: @prashant look at selector async changes, @jamal helper API, @eva post-process script. will update with new trace link ASAP :thumbsup:
